title: Mindful Minute Check-In
description: A short mindfulness reset for noticing breath, body, and mood without needing to change anything.
transcript: Arrive where you are. Let your eyes soften. Notice one breath moving in, and one breath moving out. Name what is present in the body, then let the next breath be simple.

title: Box Breathing Companion
description: A guided breathwork track that pairs with the app's box breathing reset.
transcript: Inhale for four. Hold gently for four. Exhale for four. Rest for four. Keep the effort soft and steady, following the rhythm without forcing the breath.

title: Gentle Rain
description: A looping rain soundscape for background calm during breathing, journaling, or winding down.
transcript: Ambient rain soundscape. No spoken guidance.

title: Ocean Waves
description: A soft ocean loop prepared for future ambient playback in resets and audio sessions.
transcript: Ambient ocean wave soundscape. No spoken guidance.

title: Sleep Body Scan
description: A gentle bedtime meditation for releasing tension from head to toe.
transcript: Let the day be complete for now. Bring attention to the forehead, jaw, shoulders, hands, ribs, belly, legs, and feet. Give each area permission to settle.

title: Five Senses Grounding
description: A grounding practice for reconnecting with the room when anxiety feels loud.
transcript: Name five things you can see. Four things you can feel. Three things you can hear. Two things you can smell. One thing you can taste. Let the room hold you.

title: 1-Minute Reset
description: A brief guided reset for interrupting stress and returning attention to the next small step.
transcript: Pause for one minute. Feel your feet, soften your shoulders, and notice one slow breath in. Let the breath out a little longer than it came in. Name one thing that is true right now, then choose the next kind action.

title: 3-Minute Breathing Space
description: A compact breathwork practice for checking in, gathering attention, and widening back to the body.
transcript: First, notice what is here: thoughts, feelings, and body sensations. Next, gather attention around the breath, following one inhale and one exhale at a time. Finally, widen attention to the whole body and carry that steadiness forward.

title: 5-Minute Grounding
description: A sensory grounding track for moments when anxiety feels loud or attention feels scattered.
transcript: Look around and name five things you can see. Notice four points of contact or texture. Listen for three sounds. Find two scents or neutral smells. Notice one taste, or simply the feeling of air. Let the room be enough for this moment.

title: Body Scan
description: A gentle body awareness meditation for noticing tension and practicing release without force.
transcript: Bring attention to the top of the head, then the face and jaw. Notice the neck, shoulders, arms, and hands. Move through the chest, belly, back, hips, legs, and feet. At each place, notice what is present and let the next breath make room.

title: Sleep Wind-Down
description: A slow bedtime practice for closing the day and helping the body prepare for rest.
transcript: Let the day be done for now. Notice where your body is supported. If unfinished thoughts appear, thank the mind and set them down for tomorrow. Lengthen the exhale, soften the forehead and jaw, and allow rest to arrive at its own pace.

title: Self-Compassion Pause
description: A supportive pause for responding to self-criticism with steadier, kinder language.
transcript: This is a hard moment. Hard moments are part of being human. Place a hand somewhere comfortable if that helps. Offer yourself one phrase you would say to someone you care about: may I be patient, may I be kind, may I take the next gentle step.

title: Anxiety Calming Practice
description: A guided calming practice for easing anxious activation and reconnecting with immediate safety cues.
transcript: Notice that anxiety is present, and also notice what is stable around you. Feel the support under your body. Breathe out slowly and look for three cues of safety. Let thoughts be thoughts for a few breaths, then ask what would help by one percent.
